title: Foley artists: where the name comes from and how everyday sounds are recreated for films

sources.publisher: University of Houston (Engines of Our Ingenuity)
sources.title: Episode 3009: Foley
Lost and Found Sound: The Stories (Jack Foley)
The art of Foley and sound effects secrets
The Importance of Foley Artists in Filmmaking

facts.text: Foley artists are named after Jack Foley, who worked at Universal when sound films were replacing silent films.
Jack Foley developed a way of projecting a film and adding sound effects in sync with the picture.
Footsteps were one of Jack Foley's specialties.
On a film set, microphones are placed for dialogue, so many everyday sounds are lost and must be recreated later.
Foley artists snap celery to imitate the sound of a breaking bone.
Coconut shells have long been used to imitate the hooves of a galloping horse.
Many Foley artists own large collections of shoes and pick footwear to suit each character.
Some sounds, such as car crashes and squeaky gates, are exaggerated because audiences expect them to be louder than they really are.
Alfred Hitchcock reportedly chose a melon for the knife sound in Psycho after listening to several melons with his eyes closed.
Foley sounds include footsteps, door slams and the rustle of clothing in films and TV.

notes: 混合題 mixed-advanced-02 第 1 組用（2026-10-09 線上查證，只取事實、不取原句）。Jack Foley 開始工作的年份各來源說法不一（1914、1920 年代、1929），選文不寫年份，只寫「電影開始有聲音時在 Universal 工作」。選文裡受訪的擬音師、寫專欄的影評人都是虛構人物（選文沒有寫出姓名）。
